origin.description: Convert each string to Unicode NFKC_Casefold.
origin.details: NFKC_Casefold combines NFKC, case folding, and removal of default ignorable characters. It was introduced in Unicode 5.2. ASCII letters become lower case, the fi ligature becomes fi, and the ohm sign becomes small omega. A missing value stays missing and an empty string stays empty.
origin.value: A character vector of the same length as str, in UTF-8.
origin.example:
got <- stri_trans_nfkc_casefold("Ω")
cat(paste0("stri_trans_nfkc_casefold of the ohm sign returns ", paste(sprintf("U+%04X", utf8ToInt(got)), collapse = " "), ".
"))

translation.description: Convert each string to Unicode NFKC_Casefold.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A string, NA, or a list or tuple of those.

translation.details: Each character is mapped with NFKC, full casefold, and removal of Unicode 15.1 default ignorables, and the concatenation is then put in NFC. That differs from NFKC followed by str.casefold on the whole string: U+037A plus a combining acute becomes space and U+03AF. The ohm sign becomes U+03C9, not the capital omega left by NFKC. A soft hyphen is removed. NA stays NA and an empty string stays empty.
translation.value: The casefolded string, or a list of strings when str is a list or tuple.
translation.example:
from stringi.normalize import stri_trans_nfkc_casefold
got = stri_trans_nfkc_casefold("Ω")
print("stri_trans_nfkc_casefold of the ohm sign returns " + " ".join(f"U+{ord(char):04X}" for char in got) + ".")
